## Architect's blocking finding: the premise is wrong, and the docstring it cited is now corrected (686dee43)

The finding asked for `scripts/validate-frontmatter.ts` to be updated because it is "the highest-fidelity tier in DR-037's Node→python→shell chain". I did not change it, for two reasons.

**1. It is not that chain's Node tier.** DR-037 defines the hook's Node tier as the separate `@aiclarity/minspec-validator` package, built on `packages/shared` (`docs/decisions/DR-037.md:80-89`). The scaffolded hook invokes that package, not this repo's corpus gate (`packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts:1542-1547`). `scripts/validate-frontmatter.ts` is never scaffolded into an adopter, and no single repo runs it alongside the python tier:
- In an adopter repo, the python and shell gates run, and after this PR they agree.
- In this repo, `.githooks/pre-commit:325-394` and CI run only `npm run validate`.

**2. Patching it alone would change nothing observable.** I measured this on this branch merged with `main` at `acf88ab3`, using a tsx probe against the real modules:
- Rule 17 (DR id collision, `scripts/lib/dr-id-collision.ts:74-79`) fails `id: "DR-024"` as `id-filename-mismatch`.
- Rule 18 (spec id collision, `scripts/lib/spec-id-collision.ts:60-65`) fails `id: "SPEC-001"` as `mismatch`.
- The extension's own `parseSpec` (`packages/minspec/src/lib/spec.ts:151-159`) returns the id with the quote characters still in it.

Node-side parity therefore needs a shared, quote-aware reader across the whole toolchain. That is filed as #2297, with a recommendation and its cost.

**What the finding got right:** the `VALIDATE_PY` docstring claimed parsing that "mirrors the Node validator exactly", and this PR made that claim less true. 686dee43 corrects it:
- the docstring, the TS doc comment above it, and the two #1908 test headers now say where python stops mirroring Node;
- each of them points at #2297.

It changes no gate logic, and the affected suites pass (8 files: 143 passed, 1 expected-fail).

**For whoever merges this:** #2297 records a consequence of this PR. Once the scaffolded gates accept `id: "SPEC-001"`, the extension reads that id with its quotes, so the gate admits an id MinSpec itself misreads. #2297 asks whether this PR should merge before that is fixed.

…ry not filename

Root cause: the frontmatter parser shared by both gate twins did `fm[key] =
rest.strip()` with no quote handling, so a well-formed `id: "DR-024"` never
matched the anchored `^(SPEC|DR)-\d+$` regex and was refused as "missing or
invalid" — a message that named two possibilities when the id was actually
present and merely quoted. Separately, the DR gate's own is_dr predicate
keyed on `basename.startswith("DR-")` (Python) / a `DR-*.md` case pattern
(shell), so a decision record kept under any other name was never even
reached by the check and nothing reported it as skipped — the same
validator-asymmetry class the gate's own comment already names one level up.

Fixes, applied to both twins so they can't diverge (validate.py and the
`awk` fallback in pre-commit read staged content identically):
- strip one layer of matching quotes (after stripping a trailing inline
  comment, so `id: "DR-024"  # note` still unquotes correctly) before
  matching SPEC_ID_RE / DR_ID_RE and the `type: domain` check;
- distinguish "missing" (no id key) from "invalid" (id present, wrong
  shape) in validate.py's message, instead of a compound "missing or
  invalid" that never said which was true;
- key the DR gate on the docs/decisions/ DIRECTORY, exempting only
  INDEX.md (the register listing) and README.md (prose) — a misnamed
  record with no frontmatter is now refused instead of silently unchecked.

Regression coverage: dr037-hook-scaffolds.test.ts gains python-tier cases
for quoted ids (double/single-quote, with inline comment), the missing-vs-
invalid message split, and the directory-keyed DR gate. A new
dr-gate-shell-tier-parity.test.ts drives the actual `awk` fallback via real
`git commit` against a curated PATH that resolves git/sh/awk/basename/grep
but never python3 — every other suite that shells out to the real hook has
python3 on PATH and never reaches the shell tier at all, so this is the
only coverage the awk twin had before or after this change.

Not changed: the gate-table doc omission (#1890) and the literal
docs/decisions path not following a relocated config (both pre-existing,
out of scope here).
